$description: The mode matrix. Two dimensions of two modes, so four combinations, and machinery/scripts/check-contrast.mjs resolves every declared pair in all four — a pair that is legible in light and invisible in dark is the specific failure the gate exists to catch. Base values are theme light + product market; every mode file states its values explicitly rather than relying on that, so no combination is the privileged one and light+market can be re-pointed without a hidden edit. Dimension order here is the order overrides are applied: theme first, then product, later modes winning. That order matters — see the note on text.secondary below.
$note: CROSS-DIMENSION DEPENDENCY, and how it is expressed. A mode file belongs to exactly one dimension and cannot see which mode of the other dimension is active, so a token whose value depends on both cannot be written by either file directly. text.secondary is the one such token: theme sets how light the neutral ramp runs, product picks which step of it applies. It is NOT solved with a theme.dark.product.market-style combination file — a combination takes exactly one mode from each dimension, so a combination file would have to be its own third dimension and would multiply the matrix rather than refine it. It is solved with indirection instead, which the composition rule already supports: aliases are resolved AFTER all overrides are applied, so a mode may swap a token to a different alias and the chain still resolves. Two slot tokens, text.secondary-market and text.secondary-move, are overridden by the theme dimension with the values that theme implies. The product dimension then overrides text.secondary to alias whichever slot applies. Theme runs first and sets the values; product runs second and selects. The convention, stated once so it does not have to be rediscovered: a token depending on N dimensions is expressed as one selector token plus one slot per mode of the LAST-APPLIED dimension it depends on, and the earlier dimensions set the slots. The slots are plumbing and say so in their $description; nothing outside the mode files may reference them.
